heading: How are malignant cells identified in single-cell data?
exactSourceText: There is no universal “cancer RNA” marker. Start with tissue context and a panel of cell-family markers, including suitable normal reference cells. An epithelial profile can support epithelial identity while leaving malignancy open. Check the quality of each profile: two cells captured together, RNA from nearby broken cells or sparse measurements can confuse the label.

heading: How are malignant cells identified in single-cell data?
exactSourceText: Next look for a coherent tumor-associated pattern. One research approach averages expression across neighboring genes on chromosomes to **infer large-scale copy-number alterations**. A pattern consistent with the tumor's genomic changes can support an assignment when combined with cell-family evidence. This is an inference from RNA abundance, not a direct count of DNA copies. In a primary glioblastoma study, Patel and colleagues combined inferred chromosomal patterns with expression profiles to separate probable normal cells from malignant populations. It illustrates a method in that setting, rather than a breast-cancer diagnostic rule.

heading: How a molecule becomes a count
exactSourceText: A **read** is a sequence observation. In some assays, a **unique molecular identifier (UMI)** tags a captured molecule. Repeated reads with the same tag can be collapsed, helping avoid counting amplified copies as new molecules. This estimates captured molecules under the workflow, rather than every molecule that existed in the cell.

heading: Clinical classification has its own evidence

heading: Count the copies
exactSourceText: LOH alone does not say the remaining gene is disabled. **Biallelic inactivation** asks whether neither parental copy still supplies useful function. A damaging variant on the retained copy plus loss of the other can support it, if phase and cell population fit. [Human leukocyte antigen LOH (HLA-LOH)](/wiki/education/concepts/measurement/sequencing-basics/hla-loh) applies the same copy question to immune-display genes.

heading: Account for the mixture
exactSourceText: **[Purity](/wiki/education/concepts/measurement/sequencing-basics/tumor-purity-and-ploidy)** is the fraction of sampled cells that are malignant. **Ploidy** describes genome copy content, often averaged across the genome. Methods such as ABSOLUTE estimate purity and ploidy together from the data, and more than one solution can fit ([Carter et al., 2012](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4383288/)). Keep the alternatives rather than treating one fit as a cell count. A pathologist's tissue-area [cellularity](/wiki/education/concepts/breast-cancer/surgery-and-pathology-results/tumor-bed-cellularity) estimate uses a different denominator.

heading: A worked finding: a TP53 two-hit pattern

heading: A worked finding: a TP53 two-hit pattern
exactSourceText: Count the copies in 100 cells. Sixty cancer cells each contribute one mutated copy: 60. Forty normal cells contribute 80 unmutated copies. The expected VAF is 60 ÷ 140 ≈ 43%. The data fit “every cancer cell carries the variant and has lost its other copy,” a somatic two-hit pattern.

heading: A worked finding: a TP53 two-hit pattern
exactSourceText: Now change one assumption. If purity were 86% and both copies were retained, a heterozygous variant in every cancer cell gives 86 ÷ 200 = 43% too. The same read fraction fits two different copy states. Only independent copy-number evidence chooses between them. A simpler version of this check: at 50% purity, a heterozygous variant reads 25% with both copies retained and about 33% after loss of the other copy, with no change in how many cancer cells carry it.

heading: How a molecule becomes a count
exactSourceText: A **read** is one sequence observation. heading: A worked finding: HER2-low as a delivery address
exactSourceText: The antibody–drug conjugate trastuzumab deruxtecan uses HER2 differently: as an address for delivering a chemotherapy payload, not as a growth driver to switch off. In the DESTINY-Breast04 trial (557 people with previously treated HER2-low metastatic breast cancer), median progression-free survival was 9.9 months with trastuzumab deruxtecan and 5.1 months with chemotherapy of the physician's choice, and median overall survival 23.4 versus 16.8 months ([Modi et al., 2022](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35665782/)). Only 63 participants had hormone-receptor-negative disease, so evidence specific to TNBC there is limited.

heading: A worked finding: HER2-low as a delivery address
exactSourceText: The result changed what a stain had to distinguish. HER2 IHC was built to separate overexpression (3+) from the rest, not 0 from 1+. A protein measurement is only as useful as its validation for the decision it now supports.

heading: Presence is not recognition
exactSourceText: A conventional [T-cell receptor](/wiki/education/concepts/immunology/t-cells/t-cell-receptor) reads a peptide displayed on [human leukocyte antigen (HLA)](/wiki/education/concepts/immunology/antigen-presentation/hla). Display needs a source protein, processing, [beta-2-microglobulin (B2M)](/wiki/education/concepts/immunology/antigen-presentation/b2m) and an intact HLA molecule. heading: Compare with the starting cells as well as the control
exactSourceText: [Reduction is not regression](/wiki/education/concepts/evidence-and-statistics/reasoning-tools/reduction-is-not-regression): the endpoint does not show that half the cells died. Slower division is one explanation; division balanced by death is another. Growth-rate methods correct for control growth under stated assumptions ([Hafner et al., 2016](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4887336/)). heading: Repair history is not repair now
exactSourceText: [Homologous recombination (HR)](/wiki/education/concepts/cancer-biology/genome-instability-and-repair/homologous-recombination-and-hrd) repairs certain double-strand DNA breaks using a matching template; homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) means that repair is impaired. When it fails for a long time, the genome accumulates a characteristic pattern of damage, a **genomic scar**. Scar methods summarize different features: loss of heterozygosity (LOH), telomeric allelic imbalance (TAI) and large-scale state transitions (LST), and their cutoffs are method-specific. [Mutational signatures](/wiki/education/concepts/cancer-biology/genome-instability-and-repair/mutational-signatures) are another kind of pattern.

heading: The clinical gate has a different job
exactSourceText: Even a persuasive biological chain needs treatment evidence in the disease, setting, comparator, outcome and eligibility that apply. A real example shows the gate. The OlympiA trial randomized 1,836 people with high-risk HER2-negative early breast cancer and a **germline** BRCA1 or BRCA2 variant to a year of olaparib or placebo after standard treatment. Three-year invasive disease-free survival was 85.9% versus 77.1% (hazard ratio 0.58) ([Tutt et al., 2021](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34081848/)). The approved adjuvant use follows that population, with a validated germline test.

heading: preamble

heading: The big ideas
exactSourceText: 1. **Each layer answers its own question.** [DNA, RNA and protein](/wiki/education/concepts/biology-basics/genetics/central-dogma) are related objects, not interchangeable evidence.
